questions.prompt: Why is Plaso split into log2timeline and psort as two stages?
options: They were written by different authors
Parsing is expensive and filtering is cheap -- log2timeline runs once into a storage file, and psort then queries that file repeatedly in seconds
Only one of them is still maintained
questions.explanation: Re-running log2timeline to change a date range is the most common beginner mistake, and can cost an afternoon for a result psort produces instantly.

questions.prompt: What is a bodyfile in the Sleuth Kit workflow?
options: A carved file recovered from unallocated space
The pipe-delimited intermediate format fls emits, holding MACB times per file, which mactime then converts into a sorted timeline
The output of a YARA scan
questions.explanation: fls walks the filesystem into bodyfile format and mactime renders it as a timeline -- fast, but filesystem metadata only.

questions.prompt: What timezone mistake can your own tooling introduce?
options: Plaso silently converts everything to local time
mactime requires -z explicitly and will emit local-time output if omitted, producing exactly the mixed-timezone merge error to be avoided
fls always uses the system timezone regardless of flags
questions.explanation: Mixing a UTC Plaso export with a timezone-defaulted mactime export creates a corrupted timeline from your own commands rather than from a source log.

questions.prompt: When is the Zimmerman-tools route preferable to Plaso?
options: When you already know which artifacts you need -- MFTECmd, EvtxECmd, PECmd and LECmd all emit CSV designed to load into Timeline Explorer together
questions.explanation: It is a lighter-weight route to a merged timeline that skips the expensive full-image parse when the relevant artifact set is already known.
